{"concern":"usability","lineage":"original","name":"When a design records more than one reader's background, the agent offers a guess matched to the git author, says so once, does not ask again that session — and the lens line carries each person's name beside their id so the match is a lookup","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"Anthony, 2026-09-14, promoted from dec:idea-two-readers-share-one-design-and-the-session-not-the-graph-says-which-lens-applies on his word: "Go with your suggestion for two legs and no more: skill only and lens line carries names beside ids." The case: flo2, one repo shared with his brother Alex; each should be read to in his own vocabulary, and he does not want to be asked who he is every session.

WHAT IS REQUIRED, two legs and no more:

1. THE ORIENTATION SKILL, when the design records MORE THAN ONE background: match what the harness can see — the git author name, a login, a handle — against the recorded people's names, offer the match as an assumption in one sentence ("assuming you are AJ — if not, tell me who you are and your background"), and do not ask again that session. The assumption is OFFERED, never silent (req:the-agent-learns-who-it-is-talking-to, accepted, already forbids a silent default); a correction is taken at face value and the corrected person is the reader from then on. When no recorded name matches, ask as for a new reader.

2. THE LENS LINE CARRIES NAMES BESIDE IDS: the sentence that rides every skill and loop_status reply lists "who:ajs (Anthony Sligar)" rather than the id alone, so the agent's match against the git author is a join over text already in front of it, not a hunch that needs a fetch per person. Names are already in the public export; no email or other new identity signal is recorded.

AND THE ONE RULE THAT MAKES A WRONG GUESS COST SOMETHING: the identity the agent assumes for the lens is the identity it ATTRIBUTES to — AUTHORED_BY on what it captures that session goes to the same Contributor — and it says so once. Today both answers come from the same unstated guess and a wrong one damages the record silently.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT REQUIRED, and why: the session's seat does not record the reader (the heavier option in the brainstorm); a stated assumption plus a name on every lens line already keeps a wrong guess visible and re-readable, and seat state would be built for a hosted flo2 that does not exist yet. Same machine is not same person, which is why this offers and never assumes. The persona stays per-graph.

VERIFIED BY: a served-reply test that the lens line names the person beside the id; a lint contract that the orientation skill's body states the offer-and-say-so clause; both written first and observed failing.","status":"accepted"}
